Arrows: solid = request/call, dashed orange = signed webhook,
numbered badges tie a path to its flow panel below.
Onboarding, KYC and the hosted /connect page
• Direct: owner opens /app, POST /api/signup → uk_ token. Via a developer: backend calls POST
/developer/v1/users (idempotent on externalId), then /sessions → a us_ URL on /connect (token in the
• Browser submits Card KYC to /api/me/kyc; the service forwards it to Miden kyc-submit as an Individual.
Identity data is never stored or logged; we keep only kyc_reference and status.
• Background loop polls Miden every 5 s until Approved, then POST /v2/cards/issue (reference
card-<userId>, so a retry cannot create a second card) and allocates a deposit address from the HD
• Developer gets kyc.updated and card.issued webhooks. Tier quick ($50/tx, $100/day, $500 lifetime) caps
Funding: USDC on-chain to card balance
• User sends test USDC to the per-card address on Base Sepolia (Ethereum Sepolia is also watched, since
• BaseUsdcWatcher reads Transfer logs, waits 5 blocks, credits holding:<card> (key chain+tx+logIndex, so
replays are no-ops). Sub-cent dust is never credited. Dev shortcut: simulate-deposit when
• fundPending (5 s): at $1 or more, within the tier lifetime cap, holding → pending, then Miden PATCH
/cards/topup with a stable Reference. 'Already seen' = success; 4xx releases; timeouts retry the same
• Open: the USDC received is not yet converted into the Miden USD wallet that pays the top-up. The
sandbox wallet is pre-funded. funding.completed webhook fires.
• Owner or developer creates an agent (limits clamped to the card tier), funds it from the card (ledger
card: → agent:), and hands over an ak_ token.
• Agent calls pay (MCP /mcp, stdio bridge, or POST /agent/v1/pay). AppService.pay: idempotency per
(card, agent, key) → spend row 'processing' → policy (per-tx, daily, MCC) → sub-balance debit.
• Charge: today Miden's sandbox purchase simulator (mock/authorization). Approved = approved. Definite
decline = debit reversed, voided. Lost answer = held 'processing'; reconcile matches the card's
Authorization list by a per-spend merchant id.
• Nothing from the card ever reaches the agent. spend.settled webhook fires on every final state.
• Merchant backend (SDK) signs up for mk_, creates a fixed-price checkout cs_ with a /pay/cs_ page and
• Agent calls pay_checkout. The checkout is claimed atomically and paid as an ordinary AppService.pay
under spend key checkout:<id>:<attempt>, so it is charged at most once and declined attempts can be
• We are merchant of record: on paid, ledger credits merchant:<id>. Payouts reserve first (merchant →
payout_pending), a new payout address waits 10 min in the sandbox (24 h default).
• PayoutSender signs a USDC transfer at an explicit nonce, stores the bytes, then broadcasts on Base
Sepolia; 5 confirmations = sent, revert = failed and money back. Open: merchant KYB, settlement hold,
Hosted checkout swap (agent pays any supported page)
• Agent calls pay_hosted_checkout(url, exact amount, merchant, key). Validates: swap enabled, https host
on SWAP_ALLOWED_HOSTS, amount ≤ cap ($10), card present in the vault.
• AppService.pay runs first (limits, balance, debit) under checkout:swap:<id>. Only then does
vault.reveal (audited) hand the card to the filler, as late as possible.
• Chromium loads the page, refuses on a bot check, reads the total (must equal the agreed price; re-
checked after tax/shipping steps), types the card, presses pay, watches the outcome, scrubs the details.
• Declined or never submitted = voided. Submitted without a clear answer (3DS, captcha, timeout) = held;
reconcile matches the card's Miden Authorization by amount + time and records the real MCC. Ambiguity =
• Developer sets privacyMode (default via /settings, or per user at creation). It is fixed per user.
• Each payment first passes the agent's limits and debit, then chargeCardFor issues a fresh Miden Lite
card (issue-lite) loaded with exactly the payment (minimum $1), written to app_one_time_card before the
call. Max 50 per user per day.
• The Lite card pays the merchant or the hosted checkout; its details are deleted from the vault once
the page is filled, and it ends by itself 2 days after issue.
• Known blockers: Miden caps a customer at 3 cards including Lite cards; the single-swipe rule was not
enforced by the simulator; a lost issue answer is flagged needs_review and nothing is charged.
• AppService emits events through onEvent into DeveloperService, which writes app_webhook_event (outbox)
for the owning developer. Types: kyc.updated, card.issued, funding.completed, spend.settled.
• deliverDue (in the 5 s loop, single flight) POSTs the JSON with x-agentcards-event-id and
x-agentcards-signature: t=<unix>,v1=HMAC-SHA256(whsec_, t.rawBody). 2xx = delivered; otherwise retry 30
s, 1 m, 2 m … up to 6 h, 8 tries. Redirects not followed.
• At-least-once: receivers dedupe on event id and reject t older than 5 minutes; GET
/developer/v1/events shows status and attempts. An event can be lost if the process dies before the
outbox insert, so reconcile with GET /developer/v1/users/:id.
• Inbound from Miden: not used. Signature scheme implemented, subscription blocked; KYC and balances are
• The agent holds only an ak_ token. Card PAN/CVV live encrypted in the vault, are revealed only inside
SwapService, and are scrubbed after use. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 only.
• Service binds loopback, checks the Host header (DNS-rebinding guard), and refuses cross-site POSTs.
Sandbox only: boot fails against any non-sandbox Miden URL; payout rail refuses mainnet.
• Money safety: append-only double-entry ledger with idempotency keys, row-locked daily limits, reserve-
then-settle for top-ups and payouts, and 'held, never guessed' on any lost answer.
• Production gaps recorded in the README: key custody and sweeping, USDC → Miden USD wallet funding,
customer-managed card authorization, real merchant MCC, email verification, rate limits, settlement
